brief.headline: Ask for ₹32.69 L/yr saving by matching the ₹290.00/KG price Shrinath already gives us, and trade faster payment for a further cut.

priceAsk.summary: Match the ₹290.00/KG price Shrinath Roto Pack already gives FDC on the same laminate SKUs.
priceAsk.target: ₹290.00/KG baseline (closes the ₹32.69 L/yr gap); aim for an additional cut if we pay faster.
priceAsk.basis: We already pay Shrinath ₹290.00/KG for identical Electral laminate SKUs. GEEP charges ₹294.03–308.30/KG on the same items — that's a 1.4–6.3% markup costing us ₹32.69 L/yr. The open-market asking band is ₹205–305/kg, so ₹290 sits at the fair end and is proven in our own purchase history.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Offer to pay in 15 days (half the current 30) in exchange for a price cut of roughly 4.38% (the rate they borrow at).
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Paying 15 days faster frees up ₹1.16 Cr of our cash; make sure the price cut is worth more than that to us — target at least a 4–5% reduction to break even and come out ahead.

brief.financialLeverage: They sell ₹291.36 Cr a year and keep only ₹1.1 out of every ₹100 — profit is paper-thin. Your ₹28.31 Cr order is 9.72% of everything they make, so losing you would hurt. Their cash is stuck for 81 days (suppliers wait 33d to be paid, customers take 87d to pay them) versus 46 days at similar firms, meaning cash is tight and they borrow money at rates between 1.55% and 9.25%. That tightness makes early payment very valuable to them — but the thin margin means a huge price squeeze could break them, so trade payment speed for price and keep the ask realistic.

evidence.point: GEEP charges ₹294.03–308.30/KG; Shrinath gives us ₹290.00/KG on the same SKUs
Closing the gap saves ₹32.69 L every year
We are 9.72% of their total sales — a big enough customer to demand the price Shrinath already proves is possible
Their cash is stuck for 81 days, longer than peers at 46 days, so faster payment is worth real money to them
They borrow at rates between 1.55% and 9.25%, so paying 15 days early is worth roughly 4.38% to them
Profit is only 1.1% — there's almost no fat, so push payment terms harder than price alone

alternates.name: Huhtamaki India Ltd (already supplies FDC in small volume)
alternates.why: Listed flexible-packaging converter with ₹2755.75 Cr revenue — proven, scalable second source for pharma laminate sachets; already on our books so can ramp up quickly.

alternates.name: UFLEX Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexibles giant (₹16492.00 Cr revenue) that makes both film substrate and finished laminates — can replace GEEP at any scale we need.

alternates.name: Constantia Parikh Packaging Pvt Ltd
alternates.why: Part of the global Constantia group, specializes in pharma blister and sachet laminates (₹222.04 Cr revenue) — a strong second source for GEEP's line.

risks: GEEP is 76% of our Laminates spend (₹28.31 Cr) — we have almost no backup today, so qualify Huhtamaki or UFLEX fast before pushing too hard in this meeting.

Their credit rating (CRISIL BB+ / Stable) was done without their help ('issuer not cooperating'), so the numbers may be stale — treat their financial health as uncertain and don't assume they can absorb a big hit.
They have GST filing delays, EPF payment delays and pending legal cases — watch for any sign of operational trouble that could disrupt our supply.

Profit is only 1.1% and they're burning cash (₹-1.64 Cr free cash flow) — a price cut that's too steep could tip them into real trouble and leave us scrambling for supply; balance the squeeze with supply security.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the partnership, but we're paying ₹294–308 per kilo when Shrinath already gives us ₹290 on the same laminate — let's talk about closing that gap and whether faster payment from us can earn an even better price.
